author: Thomas à Kempis
title: Of the exercises of a religious man

verses.text: The life of a Christian ought to be adorned with all virtues, that he may be inwardly what he outwardly appeareth unto men.
verses.modernizedText: The life of a Christian ought to be adorned with all virtues, so that he may be inwardly what he appears outwardly to others.

verses.text: And verily it should be yet better within than without, for God is a discerner of our heart, Whom we must reverence with all our hearts wheresoever we are, and walk pure in His presence as do the angels.
verses.modernizedText: And truly it should be even better within than without, for God discerns our heart; we must reverence Him with all our hearts wherever we are and walk pure in His presence as the angels do.

verses.text: We ought daily to renew our vows, and to kindle our hearts to zeal, as if each day were the first day of our conversion, and to say, “Help me, O God, in my good resolutions, and in Thy holy service, and grant that this day I may make a good beginning, for hitherto I have done nothing!”
verses.modernizedText: We ought daily to renew our vows and kindle our hearts to zeal, as if each day were the first day of our conversion, and to say, “Help me, O God, in my good resolutions and in Your holy service, and grant that this day I may make a good beginning, for until now I have done nothing!”

verses.text: According to our resolution so is the rate of our progress, and much diligence is needful for him who would make good progress.
verses.modernizedText: Our progress is according to our resolution, and much diligence is needed by anyone who would make good progress.

verses.text: For if he who resolveth bravely oftentimes falleth short, how shall it be with him who resolveth rarely or feebly?
verses.modernizedText: For if someone who resolves bravely often falls short, how will it be with someone who resolves rarely or feebly?

verses.text: But manifold causes bring about abandonment of our resolution, yet a trivial omission of holy exercises can hardly be made without some loss to us.
verses.modernizedText: Many causes bring about the abandonment of our resolution, yet even a small omission of holy exercises can hardly be made without some loss to us.

verses.text: The resolution of the righteous dependeth more upon the grace of God than upon their own wisdom; for in Him they always put their trust, whatsoever they take in hand.
verses.modernizedText: The resolution of the righteous depends more on the grace of God than on their own wisdom, for they always put their trust in Him, whatever they undertake.

verses.text: For man proposeth, but God disposeth; and the way of a man is not in himself.(1)
verses.modernizedText: For man proposes, but God disposes; and the way of a man is not in himself.(1)

verses.text: If a holy exercise be sometimes omitted for the sake of some act of piety, or of some brotherly kindness, it can easily be taken up afterwards; but if it be neglected through distaste or slothfulness, then is it sinful, and the mischief will be felt.
verses.modernizedText: If a holy exercise is sometimes omitted for the sake of an act of piety or brotherly kindness, it can easily be taken up afterward; but if it is neglected through distaste or sloth, then it is sinful, and the harm will be felt.

verses.text: Strive as earnestly as we may, we shall still fall short in many things.
verses.modernizedText: However earnestly we strive, we will still fall short in many things.

verses.text: Always should some distinct resolution be made by us; and, most of all, we must strive against those sins which most easily beset us.
verses.modernizedText: We should always make some definite resolution; and, above all, we must strive against those sins that most easily beset us.

verses.text: Both our outer and inner life should be straitly examined and ruled by us, because both have to do with our progress.
verses.modernizedText: We should strictly examine and govern both our outward and inward life, because both concern our progress.

verses.text: If thou canst not be always examining thyself, thou canst at certain seasons, and at least twice in the day, at evening and at morning.
verses.modernizedText: If you cannot always be examining yourself, you can do so at certain times, and at least twice a day, in the evening and in the morning.

verses.text: In the morning make thy resolves, and in the evening inquire into thy life, how thou hast sped to-day in word, deed, and thought; for in these ways thou hast often perchance offended God and thy neighbour.
verses.modernizedText: In the morning make your resolutions, and in the evening inquire into your life, how you have done today in word, deed, and thought; for in these ways you have perhaps often offended God and your neighbor.

verses.text: Gird up thy loins like a man against the assaults of the devil; bridle thine appetite, and thou wilt soon be able to bridle every inclination of the flesh.
verses.modernizedText: Gird up your loins like a man against the assaults of the devil; bridle your appetite, and you will soon be able to bridle every inclination of the flesh.

verses.text: Be thou never without something to do; be reading, or writing, or praying, or meditating, or doing something that is useful to the community.
verses.modernizedText: Never be without something to do; be reading, writing, praying, meditating, or doing something useful to the community.

verses.text: Bodily exercises, however, must be undertaken with discretion, nor are they to be used by all alike.
verses.modernizedText: Bodily exercises, however, must be undertaken with discretion, and they are not to be used by all alike.

verses.text: The duties which are not common to all must not be done openly, but are safest carried on in secret.
verses.modernizedText: Duties that are not common to all must not be done openly, but are safest carried on in secret.

verses.text: But take heed that thou be not careless in the common duties, and more devout in the secret; but faithfully and honestly discharge the duties and commands which lie upon thee, then afterwards, if thou hast still leisure, give thyself to thyself as thy devotion leadeth thee.
verses.modernizedText: But take care not to be careless in common duties and more devout in secret ones; faithfully and honestly discharge the duties and commands that lie upon you, and afterward, if you still have leisure, give yourself to yourself as your devotion leads you.

verses.text: All cannot have one exercise, but one suiteth better to this man and another to that.
verses.modernizedText: All cannot have one exercise, but one suits this person better and another suits that person.

verses.text: Even for the diversity of season different exercises are needed, some suit better for feasts, some for fasts.
verses.modernizedText: Different exercises are needed even for different seasons: some are better suited to feasts, some to fasts.

verses.text: We need one kind in time of temptations and others in time of peace and quietness.
verses.modernizedText: We need one kind in times of temptation and others in times of peace and quiet.

verses.text: Some are suitable to our times of sadness, and others when we are joyful in the Lord.
verses.modernizedText: Some are suitable for our times of sadness, and others when we are joyful in the Lord.

verses.text: When we draw near the time of the great feasts, good exercises should be renewed, and the prayers of holy men more fervently besought.
verses.modernizedText: When we draw near the time of the great feasts, good exercises should be renewed and the prayers of holy people sought more fervently.

verses.text: We ought to make our resolutions from one Feast to another, as if each were the period of our departure from this world, and of entering into the eternal feast.
verses.modernizedText: We ought to make our resolutions from one Feast to another, as if each were the time of our departure from this world and of our entrance into the eternal feast.

verses.text: So ought we to prepare ourselves earnestly at solemn seasons, and the more solemnly to live, and to keep straightest watch upon each holy observance, as though we were soon to receive the reward of our labours at the hand of God.
verses.modernizedText: So we ought to prepare ourselves earnestly at solemn seasons, live more solemnly, and keep the strictest watch over each holy observance, as though we were soon to receive the reward of our labors from God.

verses.text: And if this be deferred, let us believe ourselves to be as yet ill-prepared, and unworthy as yet of the glory which shall be revealed in us at the appointed season; and let us study to prepare ourselves the better for our end.
verses.modernizedText: And if this is delayed, let us believe ourselves still ill-prepared and still unworthy of the glory that will be revealed in us at the appointed time; and let us strive to prepare ourselves better for our end.

verses.text: Blessed is that servant, as the Evangelist Luke hath it, whom, when the Lord cometh He shall find watching.
verses.modernizedText: Blessed is that servant, as the Evangelist Luke says, whom the Lord will find watching when He comes.

verses.text: Verily I say unto you He will make him ruler over all that He hath.(2)
verses.modernizedText: Truly I say to you, He will make him ruler over all that He has.(2)
